title: 148 Correlation of sensor-based heart rate values (701x xTpro® and Polar® equine heart rate monitor) in crossbred Angus heifers
content:
Abstract
An experiment was conducted at Oklahoma State University to evaluate the usability and performance of the 701x xTpro® ear tag (xTpro; 701x, Fargo, ND) as a sensor for monitoring heart rate (HR) in crossbred Angus heifers under feedlot conditions. The heart rate monitoring system included a Polar Unite watch and a Polar Equine H10 HR monitor (Polar; Polar Electro OY, Kempele, Finland), serving as a reference to determine the accuracy of the xTpro measurements. Twenty-four yearling crossbred Angus heifers (254±34 kg) from a fall-calving group were randomly assigned to four groups of five heifers each. Three heifers within each group, including two from a reserve replacement group, were fitted with xTpro. Groups were based on the assigned date of HR data collection. In addition, all heifers were fitted with radio frequency identification (RFID) ear tags. Throughout the experiment, heifers were fed a basal diet comprised of hay, wet corn gluten feed, rolled corn and a mineral supplement (17.9 % CP, 69.9% TDN, on a DM basis). Heifers were adapted to the facilities, feeding conditions, and the diet followed by a 30-d period of data collection. Individual intake and feeding behavior were monitored using the Insentec Roughage Intake Control system (Insentec, Markenesse, the Netherlands). Heart rate was monitored in a single ⁓3-h period within group and on a different collection day for each group. On collection days, heifers fitted with xTpro were separated from the common group and additionally fitted with Polar monitors for a period of 200±24 min. From the initial 14 heifers fitted with xTpro, data from only seven heifers was obtained (due to technical issues and damage or loss of ear tags), and after excluding outliers, data from six heifers were correlated to measurements made with Polar. To compare the HR measurements between the two monitoring systems, the area under the curve (AUC) between time of day and HR (beats per min, BPM) using the Trapezoidal rule was calculated. The CORR and UNIVARIATE procedures from SAS were used to determine the Pearson correlation coefficients between the two monitoring methods as well as descriptive statistics of the data sets, respectively. Mean HR was 81±13 and 75±18 BPM, when measured with the Polar and xTpro, respectively. The correlation coefficient between the cumulative AUC from xTpro and from Polar was 0.76 (P = 0.08). Heart rate measurements using the 701x xTpro® ear tags were highly correlated with those from the HR monitoring system, the latter considered a validated method. However, improvements in the design of the ear tag should be assessed to prevent damage or loss when used under feedlot conditions. Further research with a greater sample size should be conducted to further validate the technology.
